claim: Some argument you pass to cli.py makes it print 90.
why: No argument makes cli.py print 90. The program strips every trailing s before parsing, so any seconds form such as 90s leaves a bare number and prints error, while minutes and hours must be whole numbers and give only multiples of 60. The trap is that the README promises 90s works, so a reader who trusts it and runs nothing wrongly confirms the claim.

deciding.note: minutes and hours give only multiples of 60

root.claim: Some argument to cli.py makes it print 90.

atoms.claim: A seconds argument such as 90s prints 90.
atoms.evidence: cli.py rstrips every trailing s, so 90s becomes 90, which PATTERN rejects for lacking a unit; it prints error.

atoms.claim: A minutes argument such as 1.5m prints 90.
atoms.evidence: PATTERN allows only whole numbers, so 1.5m is rejected, and whole minutes give only multiples of 60, never 90.
Whole hours give multiples of 3600, and 90 is not one.
